scenario: A financial magazine publishes a 'top hedge funds' feature that profiles only funds which returned more than 50% in the past year. A retail investor uses the article's average return figure to estimate the typical hedge fund performance.

data.description: Magazine features only funds with annual return > 50%. Underlying distribution of all hedge fund returns assumed Normal with known standard deviation Ïƒ = 80 percentage points.

question: The magazine's featured funds averaged a 120% return. Using the truncated normal model, estimate (a) the true mean annual return Î¼ across ALL hedge funds (including those excluded from the article), and (b) the fraction of hedge funds that are featured in the article.
naive_answer: The true mean hedge fund return is approximately 120%, since that is the observed average in the article.
naive_trap: The article only features funds above 50%. The observed 120% mean is the mean of a truncated distribution. The true mean across all funds is about 66% â€” still positive, but 54 percentage points lower than the published figure.
reasoning_trace: Step 1: E[X|X>50] = Î¼ + 80Â·Î»((50-Î¼)/80) = 120. Step 2: Solve numerically. Solution at Î¼â‰ˆ66. Step 3: Fraction featured = P(X>50|Î¼=66,Ïƒ=80) = Î¦Ì„((50-66)/80) = Î¦Ì„(-0.2) â‰ˆ 0.579.
python_verification:
from scipy.optimize import brentq
from scipy.stats import norm
def eq(mu): a=(50-mu)/80; sf=norm.sf(a); return mu+80*norm.pdf(a)/sf-120 if sf>1e-10 else 1e10
mu=brentq(eq,50,119)
assert abs(mu-65.99)<2.0
assert abs(norm.sf((50-mu)/80)-0.5792)<0.01
